description: Every configuration option the editor declares: persisted preferences and UI state, export options, feature flags, in-memory view options and URL flags. The source of truth for the setting: surface ids (setting:<id>). apps/canvas/test/unit/settings/storage-inventory.test.ts keeps it honest: every browser-storage call site in apps/editor (localStorage/sessionStorage getItem/setItem/removeItem/key/clear, indexedDB.open, navigator.storage.getDirectory) must be claimed by exactly one entry below (settings or excluded), and every entry's source must still hold its marker and its call sites. Tool options (<toolId>.<key>) are not listed: the gate enumerates them from the tool declarations. `sites` lists [method, first-argument expression] as written at the call site, comments ignored, whitespace collapsed.

settings.effect: Settings ▸ Models (editor ADR 290): the quantisation chosen per model and the licences acknowledged, by licence id (a changed licence asks again); read field by field (ADR 247)
the `dark` class on the editor's root element ([data-paged-editor])

the interface density: `data-density` on the editor's root element, which re-points the density tokens (control and row heights, icon size, panel padding, section spacing, the chrome bars' heights); never the canvas zoom or the document (Edit ▸ Settings ▸ Interface density; editor ADR "Density presets")

high contrast: `data-contrast` on the editor's root element ("more" for High, or for System while the operating system asks for more contrast), which re-points the theme's tokens to their high-contrast variant and draws the canvas overlays with a two-tone halo; never the document (Edit ▸ Settings ▸ Contrast; editor ADR "High contrast and AA")
the unit every geometry length is shown and read in (editor ADR 245); a typed unit converts
the active workflow mode (cockpit slots, context toolbar, panel sets); any id an editor profile registers, else the first registered mode
per mode: the right dock's open tabs and the active tab
settings.migration: the legacy dockview layout keys (paged.layout.*) are deleted on load

settings.effect: per workflow mode: the widths the left dock, the right dock and the form column were dragged to (240–480 px; a missing one is its default, 262 / 320 / 340) and whether the left dock stays pinned open on a laptop-width workspace (editor ADR "Docks are resizable and the workspace adapts")

whether the cockpit adapts to the width it is given (wide, laptop, narrow: the left dock a rail with a flyout, the docks overlays) or keeps its docks docked at every width (Edit ▸ Settings ▸ Adapt the workspace to the window; editor ADR "Docks are resizable and the workspace adapts")
per tool group: the tool its rail slot shows
the command palette's Recent group (at most five ids, newest first)

Properties' sections opened or collapsed by the user, per inspector kind (text, image, frame, page); a section not listed is open when common and collapsed when advanced (editor ADR 1217); read with a shape check (ADR 247)
the live-demo guide: collapsed to its pill or open, the bottom corner it docks to, and whether its script shows
the Export PDF dialog's form, and the options the export sends (a form stored with allPages: false reads as a range; editor ADR 1221)

the Export PDF dialog's named presets (editor ADR 1221): up to 20 entries of a name and the options a preset sets (not the pages or the profile), read entry by entry with the form's shape check (ADR 247)

File ▸ New document… opens with the setup last created (preset, size, pages, unit, bleed, margins, columns, gutter), read field by field (editor ADR 1220, ADR 247); with none stored, one page of the locale's paper

the library document open last ({ id }), reopened at the next start when the recovery journal offers nothing and nothing else opened a document; forgotten when the document is closed (UX audit F-06, editor ADR 1224; read with a shape check, ADR 247)
the image output's resolution, page scope, format and quality
how many undo steps the engine keeps (engine ADR 1030, editor ADR 285); set from the History panel, kept by the worker across loads

Edit ▸ Settings ▸ Tab hides panels (InDesign) (ADR 1201, D-03): Tab and Shift+Tab on a canvas the user clicked into toggle the panels and the tool rail instead of moving focus; stored as "true" while on, removed when off
the recorded actions the Actions panel lists and replays
settings.migration: a library of another schema version is dropped, not repaired; invalid actions are filtered out

settings.effect: "off" keeps the local document library (origin-private file system) from starting

"off" keeps the recovery journal (editor ADR 1204: checkpoints of unsaved work in the origin-private file system, and the prompt that offers a crashed session's work back) from starting; read through the editor's storage adapter
View > Editing aids > Text threads: the thread lines overlay (remembered in paged.view.editingAids)
View > Editing aids > Frame edges: the edge of every page item (remembered in paged.view.editingAids; editor ADR "Editing aids and Proof view")
View > Editing aids > Margins and columns: the margin and column guides (remembered in paged.view.editingAids)
View > Editing aids > Ruler guides: the document's ruler guides; hidden, they do not snap (UXI-GDE-004; remembered in paged.view.editingAids)
View > Editing aids > Baseline grid: the document's baseline grid (remembered in paged.view.editingAids)
View > Editing aids > Overset markers: the red plus on every frame whose story runs over (remembered in paged.view.editingAids)
View > Editing aids > Hidden characters: shown disabled, not supported yet (the engine does not report where spaces, tabs and returns are)
View > Editing aids > Nonprinting items: shown on and disabled, not supported yet (the engine always draws them on screen and leaves them out of export)
View > Snap to points: the Pen and Direct Selection snap to page edges, centre and anchors
View > Show heading anchors: the resolver's anchor badges
View > Show data markers: the data field markers overlay (editor ADR 291)
View > Outline view (cmd+y): the engine draws hairline outlines (editor ADR 287)
View > Overprint Preview: overprinting inks mix as on press instead of knocking out
View > Pixel Preview: the page as a 72 ppi raster, enlarged unsmoothed
View > Show grid: the document grid overlay
View > Show pixel grid: one line per point in Pixel Preview at 600 % and above
View > Snap to grid: gestures and the point resolver snap to the grid
View > Snap to pixel: edges and points nothing else holds land on whole points
View > Smart guides (cmd+u): alignment, spacing, angle and intersection guides
the screen mode the overlays render (W toggles Normal and Preview)
whether fill and stroke edits apply to the frame or to its text
which of the fill and stroke wells a swatch click colours
boots a single-plugin application; its chrome storage keys are scoped `.solo.<profile>`
boots the editor as a named preset of the editor profile; it wins over ?solo=
turns on per-load developer diagnostics (`debugFlag(name)`): `hits` marks hit tests, `hud` shows the viewport's developer readout (renderer, fps, cache, camera; UX audit F-21)
the live-script playground loads /scripts/<id>.js into the demo guide; `embed` starts the guide collapsed to its pill, `autoplay` plays it
the documentation iframe bridge: accepts scripts from allowed parent origins over postMessage, seeded by `seed`

View ▸ Calibrated size: this screen's density in device pixels per inch, measured in View ▸ Calibrate screen size… (a bar stretched to 10 cm or 4 in against a ruler); divided by the device pixel ratio it is the camera scale at which an inch of the document is an inch on the screen (ADR 1201 D-12, editor ADR "Navigation history and one current page"); read with a shape check (ADR 247)

settings.default: { frameEdges: false, marginsColumns: true, guides: true, baselineGrid: false, textThreads: false, oversetMarkers: true, hiddenCharacters: false, nonprinting: true }
settings.effect: the editing aids' toggles, each remembered on its own (View > Editing aids and the bottom bar's control; editor ADR "Editing aids and Proof view"); read field by field, a value that is not a boolean ignored (ADR 247)

settings.default: { gridEvery: 72, gridSubdivisions: 8, gridColor: #8fb8ff, gridsInBack: true, smart guides on, tolerancePx: 4 }
settings.effect: Guides & grid preferences: the grid's spacing, subdivisions, colour and stacking, the snap tolerance and the smart guides' options (editor ADR 287)

excluded.reason: the Tier-A model cache of the ML service (editor ADR 290): model files the user installed with consent, hash-checked; user data, not configuration (Settings ▸ Models shows and removes them).
repository sign-in: the OAuth tokens and the registered client id per server. Credentials and session state, not configuration a user sets; asserted by packages/repository's own tests.
the plugin credential store behind host.secrets (passphrase-wrapped secrets per plugin reference). User data a plugin asks for through a prompt, not an editor setting.
host.storage blob tier: plugin content bytes in the origin-private file system, not configuration.

the local document library's repositories (documents and their versions), and the recovery journal's checkpoints of unsaved work (editor ADR 1204, root paged-recovery, opened through the same opfsFs): user data, not configuration.

network grants the user remembered for a document (editor ADR 264), keyed by the identity the editor minted for it: a consent decision about one document, not configuration a user sets; asserted by test/unit/document-identity.test.ts and the bundle-host contract.
the file handles the editor recognises a reopened document by (editor ADR 264): host-held identity for remembered grants, not configuration.

the page-storage adapter (plan task E1): the store every setting above goes through when the editor's host keeps them in the page's localStorage (the app entry, createEditor `storage: "local"`). Its calls take the setting's key from the call sites listed above; it holds no key of its own.

the name the Comments panel comments as (engine ADR 1055), remembered per browser so a reviewer does not retype it: an identity convenience for new comments, not configuration (the comment itself carries the name once written).
